parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State expressions, in terms of some or all of $d$, $q$ and $V$, for:

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: the magnitude of the electric field strength

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the magnitude of the electric force acting on the nucleus

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: the kinetic energy of the nucleus when it reaches plate Y.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the change, if any, in the kinetic energy of the nucleus on reaching plate Y when the following separate changes are made.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: The distance $d$ is halved, but the p.d. $V$ remains the same.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: The nucleus is replaced by a different nucleus that is an isotope of the original nucleus with fewer neutrons.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The nucleus is carbon-14 ($^{14}_{6}\text{C}$). This nucleus decays to form a new nucleus by releasing a $\beta^{-}$ particle and only one other particle of negligible mass.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the nucleon number and the proton number of the **new** nucleus.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of the particle of negligible mass.

stem:
Two vertical metal plates are separated by a distance $d$ in a vacuum, as shown in Fig. 7.1.

{{figure:figure_7_1.png}}

Fig. 7.1 (not to scale)

The potential difference (p.d.) between the plates is $V$. A nucleus with charge $+q$ is initially at rest on plate X. The nucleus is accelerated by the uniform electric field from plate X along a horizontal path to plate Y.
